status: Presentation synthesis from Chapter 4; leaves denote hypothetical achieved attack subgoals, not proof of exploitability.

legend.OR: Any child represents an alternative route.
legend.scope: Leaves are modeled adversary actions/objectives, not experimentally proven exploit paths.

slide_notes_recommended: Derived from Chapter 4; a threat-model diagram, not experimental evidence.
Threat IDs trace to the chapter; F/NF identifiers denote relevant requirements and AS identifiers denote assumptions.
Requirements listed are relevant constraints, not assertions that every path was tested or defeated.
Cross-cutting T2, T6, T13, and T14 can appear on more than one tree.
T14 also names ledger-level and economic manipulation. The slides show coalition and governance examples; ledger agreement itself is an AS2 premise rather than an application guarantee.

trees.title: Attack tree: model-production integrity

branches.label: Abuse participant authority

leaves.label: Get an unapproved workload admitted
leaves.note: Includes genuine evidence for disallowed code and rebinding valid evidence to another identity, action key, endpoint, or deployment. Genuine hardware evidence alone is insufficient authorization.

leaves.label: Get stale authority or updates accepted
leaves.note: Reuse a consumed registration, superseded authority, or contribution from another round/deployment. Counter consumption prevents reuse, but is not proof of quote recentness.

branches.rationale: Alternative successful subgoals of the named attack surface. A leaf denotes its successful effect, not merely an attempted mutation or replay.

branches.label: Corrupt training inputs

leaves.label: Get altered data or signer roles accepted
leaves.note: Changes to signed images/annotations, substituted signer roles, or keys outside the current signer-policy snapshot are detected before training.

leaves.label: Get valid poisoned contributions accepted
leaves.note: An authorized signer or a coalition can submit attributable but semantically harmful data/updates. Equal-weight aggregation does not establish statistical benignity or resistance to coordinated poisoning.

branches.annotation: F9 · NF4; valid poisoning remains a risk
branches.rationale: Alternative successful subgoals of the named attack surface. A leaf denotes its successful effect, not merely an attempted mutation or replay.

branches.label: Corrupt the publication

leaves.label: Get substituted or stale artifacts accepted
leaves.note: Return an unrelated or stale update, global model, signature, or recipient bundle instead of the objects selected by authoritative state. Publication/parent-model context matters in addition to a valid signature.

leaves.label: Publish while omitting an accepted update
leaves.note: Omission after acceptance is the integrity arm of T6. The closed accepted set and intact measured aggregation path constrain it. Stalling before publication is shown in the availability tree.

branches.rationale: Alternative successful subgoals of the named attack surface. A leaf denotes its successful effect, not merely an attempted mutation or replay.

trees.boundary: Valid signatures establish provenance, not benign learning.
trees.notes: This tree groups the threats by attack surface. The root and intermediate nodes are attacker objectives; the leaves describe hypothetical successful misuse. Every OR node represents alternative means. Requirements are relevant controls, not attack leaves. The poison-input path remains a residual risk rather than a demonstrated rejected exploit.

trees.title: Attack tree: inference and agent integrity

branches.label: Substitute bound objects

leaves.label: Get an answer for the wrong model/input accepted
leaves.note: Cause inference for a model/input that differs from the selected finalized model tuple and receiver-issued image/job context.

leaves.label: Pass unrelated output/evidence as verified
leaves.note: Combine individually valid request, output, receipt, attestation, or model-manifest objects into a misleadingly coherent result. Verification must check their bindings.

branches.rationale: Alternative successful subgoals of the named attack surface. A leaf denotes its successful effect, not merely an attempted mutation or replay.

branches.label: Replay an earlier context

leaves.label: Get stale request/job context accepted
leaves.note: Reuse a request/job from another model, receiver run, session, or request context.

leaves.label: Get another session's receipt accepted
leaves.note: Reuse receipts or evidence across distinct contexts. The chapter explicitly does not exclude same-context replay within the issue-time window.

branches.rationale: Alternative successful subgoals of the named attack surface. A leaf denotes its successful effect, not merely an attempted mutation or replay.

branches.label: Manipulate the agent

leaves.label: Get an unverified answer accepted via injection
leaves.note: Prompt injection or misleading metadata attempts to make the agent bypass mandatory verification. The actual acceptance decision belongs to deterministic services.

leaves.label: Get spoofed tool identity/output accepted
leaves.note: Tool-name conflicts or fabricated outputs attempt to mislead the bounded workflow. This is a modeled attempt, not proof that the service checks can be bypassed.

branches.rationale: Alternative successful subgoals of the named attack surface. A leaf denotes its successful effect, not merely an attempted mutation or replay.

trees.boundary: Receipt checks do not independently authenticate the Intel quote chain.
trees.notes: The chapter states that per-call verification checks internal signatures and bindings but does not authenticate the individual quote signature/Intel chain. Hardware attribution depends on earlier admission of the registry-bound receiver. Recentness is not challenge-based replay protection. These slide statements describe Chapter 4, not any later implementation-specific external audit.
trees.goal: Accept a misbound or unverified result

trees.title: Attack tree: progress and auditability

branches.label: Stop successful completion

leaves.label: Stall or withhold aggregation
leaves.note: Stop progressing, refuse enough eligible updates, or withhold publication. This is the availability arm of T6; omission from an accepted set is shown in the integrity tree.

leaves.label: Make shared infrastructure unavailable
leaves.note: Exhaust or make ledger, storage, network, inference, UI, or other shared services unreachable beyond the targeted aggregator-recovery path.

branches.annotation: F2 · NF2; no global availability guarantee
branches.rationale: Alternative successful subgoals of the named attack surface. A leaf denotes its successful effect, not merely an attempted mutation or replay.

branches.label: Disrupt the audit trail

leaves.label: Suppress results or required evidence
leaves.note: Release success without a receipt, omit a complete verified domain bundle, or suppress the entire interaction. Publication before receiver success cannot prove calls that never reached/completed at the receiver.

leaves.label: Block log writes or present conflicting views
leaves.note: Refuse a record, return invalid inclusion or ordering evidence, or provide inconsistent views. Exact-byte verification addresses invalid statements, whereas detecting a colluding split view needs witnesses/anchoring outside the prototype.

branches.rationale: Alternative successful subgoals of the named attack surface. A leaf denotes its successful effect, not merely an attempted mutation or replay.

branches.label: Force unjustified recovery

leaves.label: Reach the eligible-reporter threshold
leaves.note: Collect admissible reports from enough distinct eligible non-aggregator identities to meet the configured threshold. By itself this can describe justified recovery; identity admission does not prove that reporters are independent.

leaves.label: Make those reports falsely allege failure
leaves.note: The same report set falsely alleges failure of a healthy aggregator. False reports alone may remain below the threshold. Both leaves refer to the same current round and selected aggregator, and all reports must satisfy the contract timing and reportability conditions.

branches.note: Both properties must hold for the same report set: sufficient eligible reports and a false allegation against a healthy aggregator. The threshold alone can represent justified recovery; false reports alone may remain below the threshold. This AND is a conjunction of conditions, not a temporal sequence.
branches.annotation: T14; quorum does not prove independence
branches.rationale: Both properties must hold for the same report set: sufficient eligible reports and a false allegation against a healthy aggregator. The threshold alone can represent justified recovery; false reports alone may remain below the threshold. This AND is a conjunction of conditions, not a temporal sequence. The model presupposes all other contract eligibility, timing, and reportability conditions. The chapter treats sufficiently broad collusion as outside its general application-level guarantees.

trees.boundary: Targeted recovery does not guarantee global availability or log consistency.
trees.notes: The root is OR because disrupting progress, auditability, or coordination is sufficient for this high-level adversary objective. Only the unjustified-recovery branch is AND. Successful replacement tests do not demonstrate resistance to colluding voters or permanent shared-infrastructure outages.

trees.title: Attack tree: models, keys and trust roots

branches.label: Abuse model distribution

leaves.label: Recover a key outside the recipient set
leaves.note: Obtain a model key through the intended publication/recovery path without being an eligible recipient. Public ciphertext downloads alone do not constitute disclosure.

leaves.label: Obtain plaintext through unauthorized access
leaves.note: Obtain a plaintext model or service-local secret through the intended distribution path. Subsequent redistribution by an authorized plaintext recipient is explicitly outside the guarantee.

branches.annotation: F7; recipient redistribution is out of scope
branches.rationale: Alternative successful subgoals of the named attack surface. A leaf denotes its successful effect, not merely an attempted mutation or replay.

branches.label: Compromise secret custody

leaves.label: Extract private or process keys
leaves.note: Extract participant, process, medical-signer, receiver, or other protected private keys. The corresponding guarantees depend on protected key custody.

leaves.label: Misuse live keys inside a compromised workload
leaves.note: Use protected key material for unauthorized operations after compromising its workload. A process exploit alone does not establish this leaf; actual secret misuse is required. Additional signatures do not repair a compromised signer.

branches.rationale: Alternative successful subgoals of the named attack surface. A leaf denotes its successful effect, not merely an attempted mutation or replay.

branches.label: Defeat the roots of trust

leaves.label: Break cryptographic or hardware trust
leaves.note: Break a selected primitive or defeat the measured-execution/attestation root. This is an explicit premise boundary, not an exploit countered by an application-level test.

leaves.label: Compromise governance authority
leaves.note: Compromise governance keys or coordinate policy abuse. Correct policy configuration, signer governance, and intact protected principals remain assumptions.

branches.rationale: Alternative successful subgoals of the named attack surface. A leaf denotes its successful effect, not merely an attempted mutation or replay.

trees.boundary: Protection ends at compromised roots or authorized plaintext redistribution.
trees.notes: The broad root intentionally includes both confidentiality and key-trust compromise: a defeated signing/attestation root can violate integrity even before disclosure occurs. T5 describes the intended encrypted-distribution boundary; T13 marks explicit trust premises; governance collusion is part of T14. These are distinct from clinically incorrect but correctly signed data.
trees.goal: Expose secrets or defeat trust roots
